risks.title: Risk of Costs Exceeding Contractual Revenues
risks.score_rationale: The risk is described as potentially leading to expenses significantly exceeding contract revenues, with strong language (meaningful risk). It represents a material, albeit isolated, existential risk that is not mitigated. Litigation category heavily weighted.

risks.title: Increased Exposure to Intellectual Property Warranties
risks.score_rationale: The document notes a rising risk related to IP warranties due to the current legal climate. Although past payments have been low, the trend is upward. Litigation category highly weighted.

risks.title: Growing Long-Term Funding Commitments
risks.score_rationale: Commitments increased from $105M to $179M in one year (70%), indicating greater exposure to customer credit risk. Explicit mention of default risk. Credit category significant.

risks.title: Subjective Assessment of Long-Term Contract Costs
risks.score_rationale: This risk is central in the Critical Accounting Estimates section, with direct impact on financial results. Estimating future costs is complex and subject to adjustments. Highly technical language used.

risks.title: Risk of Actuarial Assumptions Being Invalidated
risks.score_rationale: A 25 basis point change in discount or return rates has a material impact (up to $111M). Although assumptions are reviewed annually, they remain sensitive to market conditions.

risks.title: Concentration Risk on Goodwill Value
risks.score_rationale: Goodwill is subject to annual impairment tests, but a change in conditions could lead to material write-downs. Explicit mention of significant impact on financial statements.

risks.title: High Long-Term Cash Obligations
risks.score_rationale: Over $9.5 billion in long-term obligations ($9.518B, of which $8.476B is debt), primarily debt. Financing relies on operating cash flow or new borrowings, exposing the company to liquidity risk.

ai_positioning.summary: Motorola Solutions references AI-driven capabilities across its three technology areas (MCN, Video, Command Center) but without quantifiable operational details. AI is positioned as an integrated capability rather than a standalone strategic pillar.
evidence: AI-powered capabilities mentioned in MCN (software and infrastructure)
AI-powered analytics in Video (video management and monitoring)
AI-powered capabilities in Command Center (workflow enhancement)
